title: From Recovery To Self-Reliance
subtitle:
A Journey Of Renewed Hope
NAPDDR Facilitates Rehabilitation, Sustainable Livelihood and Financial Independence for a Beneficiary in Bagalkot Karnataka
body_text: The journey of a 45-year-old resident of Bagalkot district, Karnataka Mr Raja (name changed) highlights the importance of integrating medical treatment, counselling and rehabilitation with livelihood assistance to facilitate the social and economic reintegration of individuals recovering from substance dependence. Through NAPDDR, efforts are being made to support affected individuals in overcoming addiction-related challenges and leading productive and dignified lives. For individuals facing substance dependence, access to timely medical treatment, counselling, rehabilitation and livelihood opportunities can play a significant role in rebuilding their lives and restoring social and economic stability. For Raja, overcoming alcohol dependence marked an important step towards leading a healthier, more stable and dignified life. Despite the challenges associated with alcohol dependence, Raja remained determined to rebuild his life, secure meaningful employment and ensure a better future for his family. His aspirations for financial independence and family well-being encouraged him to seek professional support and work towards recovery. The National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, seeks to address substance dependence through preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration of affected individuals. With support under NAPDDR, Raja received counselling, medical treatment and healthcare assistance at Sri Maitri District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC), Vidyagiri, Bagalkot, Karnataka. The intervention helped him progress towards recovery, rebuild his confidence and explore opportunities for sustainable livelihood and social reintegration. Through continued guidance and job placement assistance provided by the centre, Raja was encouraged to pursue employment in hospital laboratory services. The support enabled him to translate his aspirations for financial independence into meaningful employment. Raja has since secured employment as a Lab Technician at a hospital and is currently earning approximately ₹30,000 per month. The opportunity has provided him with a regular source of income, greater financial stability and an improved ability to contribute to his family's well-being. Raja’s journey highlights the importance of integrating medical treatment, counselling and rehabilitation with livelihood assistance to facilitate the social and economic reintegration of individuals recovering from substance dependence. Through NAPDDR, efforts are being made to support affected individuals in overcoming addiction-related challenges and leading productive and dignified lives. His experience reflects how timely intervention, institutional support and sustainable employment opportunities can help individuals move beyond substance dependence towards renewed hope, financial independence, social reintegration and self-reliance. *** SS-196-TAR/KV/GA/RK
